rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3, two-season (2016-17, 2017-18) randomized block field experiment with five irrigation treatments on tomato at Gosaba, West Bengal. Q2: Table 4 and Section 3.2, drip at 100% ET0 gave 56.51 t/ha and drip 80% ET0 53.00 t/ha versus 43.37 t/ha under surface irrigation; drip with or without mulch significantly raised fruits per plant and fruit yield. Q4: Table 9 and Section 3.7, post-harvest soil EC lowest under drip treatments and highest under surface irrigation (the salinity-driven water shortage identified as the yield constraint); Table 12, profile water contribution and total water use measured per treatment.
rows.notes: Study is under coastal saline/dry-season water-scarce conditions rather than drought per se; the yield gain of drip is relative to surface furrow irrigation. Single site, single cultivar (NS 501), plot scale (4 x 3 m). Only DMRT letter groupings reported, no SD/SE/CI. Limitations stated concern only the soil-EC effect being restricted to topsoil, not the yield result. Q4 is a lenient call: soil moisture regime is asserted, but soil EC and water-balance components were measured.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3, two-season field experiment with surface and drip treatments on tomato. Q2: Table 12 and Section 3.8, drip at 80% ET0 (with or without mulch) applied about 236 and 223 mm versus 300 mm under surface irrigation, with lowest total water use and highest water productivity (182-186 kg/ha-mm) in drip 80% ET0 + mulch versus 105-116 under surface irrigation.
rows.notes: Water saving is shown directly through applied-water accounting; note that drip at 100% ET0 applied nearly the same volume as surface irrigation (295/278 vs 300 mm), so the saving arises mainly from deficit (80% ET0) scheduling and mulch. The mechanisms (reduced evaporation, deep percolation) are asserted from literature, not measured. One site, one crop, plot scale; no dispersion statistics; no stated limitations of the water-use result.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3, two-year field trial with a drip 80% ET0 + straw mulch treatment on tomato. Q2: Table 4 and Section 3.2, drip 80% ET0 + straw mulch gave the significantly highest fruit yield (61.67 t/ha) and marketable yield (60.32 t/ha), versus 43.37 t/ha for surface irrigation and 53.00 t/ha for drip 80% ET0 without mulch. Q4: Table 9, lowest topsoil EC (2.10 dS/m) under drip + mulch versus 3.61 under surface; Table 12, profile water contribution and total water use measured per treatment; Table 5, leaf N, K and chlorophyll highest in drip + mulch.
rows.notes: Supports the passage directly. Single site, one cultivar, plot scale, two seasons; only DMRT letters, no SD/SE/CI. Interaction year x treatment non-significant for yield. Limitations stated relate only to the EC effect being confined to the top-soil layer.
